title: Name and explain intermediate operations (filter, map, sorted, distinct, limit, skip, peek) and that they are lazy.

s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Intermediate operations transform a Stream into another Stream and are ALL lazy — they execute only when a terminal operation triggers the pipeline. Two categories: STATELESS (filter, map, flatMap, peek) — process each element independently, O(1) memory, order-independent. STATEFUL (sorted, distinct, limit, skip) — must see multiple/all elements before producing output, O(n) memory for sorted/distinct.

| Operation | Signature | What it does | Stateful? |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|-----------|
| `filter` | `Stream<T> → Stream<T>` | Keep matching elements | Stateless |
| `map` | `Stream<T> → Stream<R>` | Transform each element | Stateless |
| `flatMap` | `Stream<T> → Stream<R>` | Transform + flatten (1-to-many) | Stateless |
| `peek` | `Stream<T> → Stream<T>` | Side-effect (debug only) | Stateless |
| `sorted` | `Stream<T> → Stream<T>` | Sort all elements | **Stateful** (buffers ALL) |
| `distinct` | `Stream<T> → Stream<T>` | Remove duplicates | **Stateful** (HashSet) |
| `limit` | `Stream<T> → Stream<T>` | Take first n | **Stateful** (counter) |
| `skip` | `Stream<T> → Stream<T>` | Drop first n | **Stateful** (counter) |

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Think of a bank's cheque processing line with 8 stations:

**filter** = the verification clerk who checks "is this cheque valid?" — invalid cheques are removed from the line. **map** = the exchange counter that converts USD cheques to INR amounts. **flatMap** = the bulk-cheque splitter: one corporate cheque becomes 50 individual salary cheques. **sorted** = the sorting machine that arranges all cheques by amount (must collect ALL before sorting). **distinct** = the duplicate detector that removes re-submitted cheques. **limit** = "only process the first 10 cheques today." **skip** = "skip the first 5 — they were already processed yesterday." **peek** = the CCTV camera recording each cheque for audit — it watches but changes nothing.

**One line to remember:** filter=keep, map=transform, flatMap=transform+flatten, sorted=sort(buffers all), distinct=unique(HashSet), limit=take-n, skip=drop-n, peek=debug. ALL lazy until terminal.

sections.s3_banking:
**Problem — The bank's monthly statement generator needs a pipeline that:** filters active transactions, maps to display format, flattens sub-transactions (flatMap), removes duplicates (distinct), sorts by date descending, paginates with skip/limit, and logs each step (peek). The old code had 8 separate for-loops. The team builds ONE stream pipeline using all 8 intermediate operations.

**What the project will show:** Every intermediate operation in one realistic pipeline, stateless vs stateful behavior, flatMap flattening nested structures, skip+limit for pagination, and peek for debugging.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** Rajesh's account has 10 transactions loaded from DB.

**Step 2 — filter(isCompleted).** 10 → 8. Removes TXN-005 (DUPLICATE status) and TXN-009 (FAILED status). Stateless: checks one element at a time.

**Step 3 — peek.** Logs each of the 8 remaining transactions. No modification. Debug only.

**Step 4 — distinct().** 8 → 7. TXN-003 and TXN-005 had same description+amount+date (BigBazaar Rs.3500 on Jan 7). But TXN-005 was already removed by filter. If both had COMPLETED status, distinct would remove the second. Stateful: maintains internal HashSet of seen elements.

**Step 5 — sorted(date DESC).** Buffers all 7 elements, sorts by date descending. Jan 25 (dividend) first, Jan 1 (salary) last. Stateful: O(n) memory.

**Step 6 — skip(0).limit(5).** Page 0: skip 0, take 5. Returns Jan 25, Jan 20, Jan 18, Jan 15, Jan 10. Stateful counter.

**Step 7 — map(toLineItem).** Transforms each Transaction entity to LineItem DTO with date, description, type, amount, category.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ ALL 8 INTERMEDIATE OPS IN ONE PIPELINE ═══

  Source: 10 transactions from DB
    │
    ▼ filter(isCompleted)                    [STATELESS, O(1)]
    │ 10 → 8 (removed DUPLICATE, FAILED)
    │
    ▼ peek(log each)                         [STATELESS, O(1)]
    │ 8 → 8 (unchanged, just logs)
    │
    ▼ distinct()                             [STATEFUL, O(n) HashSet]
    │ 8 → 7 (removed duplicate BigBazaar)
    │
    ▼ sorted(date DESC, amount DESC)         [STATEFUL, buffers ALL 7]
    │ 7 → 7 (reordered: Jan25, Jan20, Jan18, Jan15, Jan10, Jan07, Jan05, Jan01)
    │
    ▼ skip(page × pageSize)                  [STATEFUL, counter]
    │ 7 → depends on page (page=0: skip 0)
    │
    ▼ limit(pageSize)                        [STATEFUL, short-circuit counter]
    │ → takes first 5 (page=0)
    │
    ▼ map(Transaction → LineItem)            [STATELESS, O(1)]
    │ 5 Transaction entities → 5 LineItem DTOs
    │
    ▼ toList()                               [TERMINAL]
    └── Result: List<LineItem> with 5 items

  ═══ FLATMAP — FLATTEN NESTED STRUCTURE ═══

  Without flatMap:
    accounts.stream().map(Account::getTransactions)
    → Stream<List<Transaction>>  ← NESTED! Can't filter individual txns!

  With flatMap:
    accounts.stream().flatMap(a → a.getTransactions().stream())
    → Stream<Transaction>  ← FLAT! Each txn is a top-level element!

    Account SAV2001 → [TXN-001, TXN-002, ..., TXN-010]  ← 10 txns
    Account CUR3001 → [TXN-011, TXN-012]                 ← 2 txns
    flatMap → [TXN-001, TXN-002, ..., TXN-010, TXN-011, TXN-012]  ← 12 flat

  ═══ STATELESS vs STATEFUL ═══

  STATELESS (O(1) memory):          STATEFUL (O(n) memory):
  ├─ filter   — checks one          ├─ sorted   — buffers ALL
  ├─ map      — transforms one      ├─ distinct — HashSet of seen
  ├─ flatMap  — expands one         ├─ limit    — counter
  └─ peek     — observes one        └─ skip     — counter
```

  4.     → .filter(COMPLETED)                      STATELESS O(1)

sections.s6_takeaway:
Intermediate operations are lazy transformations that build a pipeline description and return a new Stream. They fall into two categories: stateless operations like filter, map, flatMap, and peek process each element independently with O(1) memory. Stateful operations like sorted, distinct, limit, and skip require knowledge of multiple or all elements: sorted buffers the entire stream before emitting, distinct maintains an internal HashSet of seen elements, and limit/skip use counters. All eight are lazy — they execute only when a terminal operation triggers the pipeline.

In my statement generator service, I chain all eight intermediate operations in one pipeline: filter removes non-completed transactions, peek logs for debugging, distinct removes duplicate entries using custom equals and hashCode, sorted arranges by date descending, skip and limit implement pagination, and map transforms entities to DTOs. The key operation I highlight is flatMap: when generating a cross-account statement, each Account has a List of Transactions. Without flatMap, `map(Account::getTransactions)` produces `Stream<List<Transaction>>` — a nested structure you cannot filter or sort. With flatMap, `flatMap(a -> a.getTransactions().stream())` produces `Stream<Transaction>` — a flat stream where each transaction is a top-level element.

The practical distinction between stateless and stateful matters for performance. Stateless operations work with infinite streams because they process one element at a time. Stateful operations like sorted on an infinite stream cause an infinite hang or OutOfMemoryError because they must see all elements before producing output. Distinct on an infinite stream works technically (it maintains a growing HashSet) but eventually runs out of memory. Limit is stateful but short-circuiting — it stops the pipeline after n elements, making it safe for infinite streams. Understanding these categories helps you order operations optimally: filter before sorted reduces the number of elements sorted, and limit before sorted is pointless because sorted needs all elements anyway.
